title: Classic Nigerian Jollof Rice
description: The legendary smoky, rich, and spicy party Jollof rice.
steps: Blend tomatoes, tatashe, scotch bonnet, and onions into a smooth paste. Boil until water evaporates.
In a large pot, heat vegetable oil and fry diced onions until translucent.
Add tomato paste and fry for 5 minutes to remove the sour taste.
Pour in the boiled pepper mix, add maggi, salt, thyme, curry powder, and bay leaves. Fry for 10-15 minutes.
Wash the rice thoroughly to remove excess starch. Stir the rice into the stew base.
Add meat stock and just enough water to sit slightly below the rice level. Cover tightly with foil to trap steam.
Cook on very low heat for 45 minutes until the rice is tender and slightly burns at the bottom for that party smokiness.

title: Egusi Soup with Bitterleaf
description: A rich and hearty melon seed soup packed with assorted meats and bitterleaf.
steps: Boil beef, goat meat, and shaki with onions, maggi, and salt until tender.
Blend the egusi seeds with a little water or onion to form a thick paste.
In a separate pot, heat palm oil (do not bleach). Add chopped onions and fry slightly.
Add the egusi paste and fry for about 10 minutes until it forms clumps.
Pour in the meat stock, add the boiled meats, dry fish, stockfish, and crayfish. Let it boil for 15 minutes.
Wash the bitterleaf properly to reduce bitterness and add it to the soup. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with pounded yam, garri (eba), or fufu.

title: Ewa Agoyin
description: Extremely soft mashed beans served with a dark, spicy, caramelized pepper sauce.
steps: Pick and wash the beans. Boil with plenty of water until extremely soft. Add salt when it's almost done and mash to a paste.
Blend dried tatashe, cameroon pepper, and lots of onions roughly. Drain excess water.
Heat a generous amount of palm oil in a pot until it bleaches (turns clear and looks like vegetable oil - do this in a well-ventilated area).
Add sliced onions to the bleached oil and fry until they turn dark brown/black.
Add the blended pepper mix and fry continuously on medium-low heat for 30-45 minutes until the sauce is very dark, gritty, and oil floats to the top.
Add crayfish, maggi, and salt to taste. Serve the sauce poured generously over the mashed beans with Agege bread.

title: Catfish Pepper Soup
description: Point and kill! A spicy, watery broth made with fresh catfish and aromatic spices.
steps: Wash the cut catfish thoroughly with hot water or alum to remove the slime.
Place the fish in a pot, add water just enough to cover it.
Blend scotch bonnet, onions, and scent leaves and add to the pot.
Add pepper soup spice (ehuru, uziza), crayfish, maggi, and salt.
Boil on medium heat for 15-20 minutes until the fish is cooked but not scattered.
Serve hot with boiled yam, plantain, or cold drinks.

title: Akara (Bean Cakes)
description: Deep-fried bean batter, light, fluffy on the inside and crispy outside.
steps: Soak beans for 10 minutes and peel off the skin (or use a blender to pulse-peel). Wash until completely clean.
Blend the peeled beans with very little water, scotch bonnet, and onions until very smooth.
Pour batter into a bowl and use a whisk or mortar and pestle to beat it for 5 minutes. This incorporates air and makes it fluffy.
Add salt to taste just before frying. Do not add water.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan. Scoop the batter into the hot oil in small portions.
Fry until golden brown on all sides. Serve hot with pap (akamu) or bread.
